compiled_state.title: [brainstorm/cross-epic-scan]: 19-epic batches force agents to issue 19 ticket-show calls -> sub-agent context auto-compact mid-scan returns summary-only output and hallucinated content
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** eb487f27517f0608e82c6424b0f1a887b035d895
* **Affected component:** plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/prompts/cross-epic-scan.md (batch sizing); plugins/dso/agents/cross-epic-interaction-classifier.md (per-batch context budget); orchestrator dispatch loop in brainstorm/SKILL.md Phase 2 Step 2.25
* **Observed during:** brainstorm session 2026-05-15 (per-story LLM review epic), 10 batches × 19 epics each dispatched in parallel against 186 open candidate epics

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

The cross-epic interaction classifier agent (dso:cross-epic-interaction-classifier, haiku-tier) should classify each batch of open epics against the new epic and return a structured `interaction_signals` JSON output per its agent contract. Output should be deterministic structured JSON regardless of batch-size.

#### Actual Behavior

For batches larger than ~10 epics, sub-agents hit Anthropic context-window auto-compaction mid-run. Observable signatures during this session:

| Batch | Duration | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 8 (19 epics) | 43s | Clean structured JSON |
| 10 (15 epics) | 84s | Clean structured JSON |
| 7 (19 epics) | 138s | Summary only — no JSON surfaced |
| 9 (19 epics) | 165s | 'JSON written to stdout per agent contract' — JSON not actually present |
| 6 (19 epics) | 199s | Confused output — conflated new_epic with content from a different ticket (3b8b) |
| 2 (19 epics) | 298s | Summary only |
| 3 (19 epics) | 1,153s (~19 min) | Returned JSON but ran extraordinarily long |

Root cause hypothesis: cross-epic-scan.md instructs the agent to perform N ticket-show calls (one per open epic) per batch. With N=19 and each ticket-show JSON being ~2-10KB, per-agent context climbs into 100K+ territory. When auto-compaction fires mid-run, the agent's narrative reasoning is retained while the precise input data (ticket descriptions, the new_epic JSON) is summarized out. Subsequent reasoning then hallucinates: agents return narrative summaries instead of structured JSON, or confuse the new epic's content with another ticket's content that was loaded during their session.

The compaction is silent — the agent doesn't know its context was compacted, so it confidently produces degraded output that the orchestrator must filter for quality.

### 3. Action History

Session ran /dso:brainstorm Step 2.25 cross-epic interaction scan against 186 open candidate epics. Partitioned into 10 batches of 19 (one batch of 15). All 10 dispatched in parallel via Agent tool calls (haiku model). 7 of 10 returned degraded output as documented above.

Workaround applied during this session: accepted partial signal set per the cross-epic-scan.md fallback contract ('Partial signal sets are acceptable. Do not let classifier failures block the brainstorm workflow.'). Continued the brainstorm with the signals from cleanly-returning batches.

### 4. Chronological Rationalization

The cross-epic-scan.md protocol caps batches at 'up to 20 epics each' — that cap reflected the haiku context budget at the time it was written, but the per-epic ticket descriptions have grown over time (many epics now have detailed Context/Approach sections plus 5-7 SCs each), pushing per-batch context past the haiku auto-compaction threshold. The protocol cap is now obsolete relative to current ticket sizes.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* **Affected workflow step:** /dso:brainstorm Phase 2 Step 2.25 (Cross-Epic Interaction Scan, HARD GATE — substitutions prohibited)
* **Affected files:** plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/prompts/cross-epic-scan.md; plugins/dso/agents/cross-epic-interaction-classifier.md
* **Proposed mitigation:** Reduce batch-size cap from 20 (currently 19 used in practice) to 5 epics per batch. With 5 × 5-10KB ticket-show outputs ≈ 25-50KB per batch, well below haiku auto-compaction threshold. Additional consideration: orchestrator may also pre-load all ticket descriptions to /tmp JSON files and pass file paths to agents, so agents skip the ticket-show calls entirely. Both mitigations are compatible.
* **Downstream effect of fix:** 186-epic candidate sets would produce ~38 batches instead of 10. Parallel dispatch (MAX_AGENTS=unlimited) handles this fine; sequential dispatch (MAX_AGENTS=1) would serialize the scan over ~38× longer but still complete reliably.
